name: PAD Amputation Re-amputation and Mortality — Synthetic Data Module (pad_amp v2)
remarks: PURPOSE
Adds amputation PROGRESSION signal to the pad_amp dataset for pad-bka-aka-prog,
the external validation of AMPREDICT MoRe (Norvell et al., Eur J Vasc Endovasc
pad_amp v1 has ZERO re-amputation signal — all 198 index-amputation patients
have exactly one amputation date — and 1 year mortality of only 4.0%. This
module supplies the missing half of MoRe's 2x2 outcome.
THE POINT OF THIS MODULE IS TO MAKE A WRONG COHORT SQL FAIL
MoRe's incident-level and re-amputation logic CANNOT be expressed in circe:
it classifies on TIMING and ANTECEDENT, not set membership (see
pad-bka-aka-prog docs/MODEL_RECREATION.md 14 entry 17). That study must
therefore hand-author its cohort SQL, and hand-authored cohort SQL is the
riskiest code in it.
So this module deliberately emits NEGATIVE CONTROLS as well as signal: events
that a naive implementation will wrongly count. If the pre-flight passes
whether the SQL is right or wrong, the dataset has failed at its job.
The negative controls are:
- re-amputations INSIDE the exclusion window (must not count)
- CONTRALATERAL amputations (must not count)
- guillotine closures at >3 weeks (must recode, not classify the level)
- toe and RAY amputations (never an incident level, never a re-amputation)
PUBLISHED TARGETS — all verbatim from the MoRe fulltext, 2026-08-06
INCIDENT LEVEL MIX, of 9 221 incident unilateral amputations (Results,
'Summary of sample'):
(14 143 identified, 4 922 = 34.8% excluded)
NOTE: the level mix belongs to the BASE module, which owns the index event.
It is recorded here because this module's routing depends on it.
FOUR CATEGORY OUTCOME, development sample n = 7 376 (Results, 'Summary of
outcomes distribution'; Table 1). This module is driven directly off the JOINT
distribution so the marginals cannot drift:
ND/NR  4 254  57.7%   no death, no re-amputation
ND/R   1 690  22.9%   no death, re-amputation
D/NR   1 056  14.3%   death, no re-amputation
D/R      376   5.1%   death AND re-amputation
Implied marginals: death 19.4%, re-amputation 28.0% (v1 has 4.0% and 0%).
MoRe's RE-AMPUTATION DEFINITION, verbatim (Methods, 'Outcomes')
'Re-amputation was identified by an amputation procedure code that occurred
1 - 365 days after the definitive incident amputation (or 22 - 365 days after
guillotine or disarticulation procedures to allow for revisions within three
weeks) and was ipsilateral to the incident procedure, had unknown laterality,
or was bilateral at the same or higher level than the incident amputation.'
FOUR THINGS THERE THAT ARE EASY TO GET WRONG, all exercised by this module:
1. TWO windows, not one: 1-365 d after a DEFINITIVE index, but 22-365 d
after a GUILLOTINE or DISARTICULATION index. A single 1-365 rule
over-counts; a single 22-365 rule under-counts.
2. UNKNOWN laterality COUNTS, and so does BILATERAL. Only a confirmed
contralateral event is excluded. An implementation that requires
laterality = ipsilateral will under-count.
3. SAME OR HIGHER level only. A more distal subsequent amputation is not a
re-amputation.
4. 'It is understood that re-amputation and death could only be counted if
the re-amputation preceded death.' The D/R stratum REQUIRES re-amp date
< death date. This module enforces that ordering.
THREE RE-AMPUTATION SUB-TYPES, all counted (Methods, 'Outcomes'):
a. soft tissue revisions      — TT and TF only
b. re-amputation, same level  — TT and TF only
c. definitive at higher level — e.g. TM->TT, TT->TF
TM SPECIAL CASE, verbatim: 'Because TM amputations do not have codes for
soft tissue revision or re-amputation at the same level, all TM codes after
an incident TM amputation were coded as a subsequent TM amputation and
classified as a re-amputation at the same level.'
** Note 'all TM codes' — BROADER than the ICD-9 84.3 route recorded in
pad-bka-aka-prog 14 entry 18. Any subsequent TM-level code qualifies. **
TWO OPEN PROBLEMS. READ BEFORE GENERATING.
1. TODO [VOCAB] GUILLOTINE HAS NO SNOMED CONCEPT. Verified against local
omop_vocab 2026-08-06: the only guillotine-amputation concepts are CPT4 —
27882 'Amputation, leg, through tibia and fibula; open, circular
(guillotine)' (OMOP 2105448, standard) and 27592 'Amputation, thigh,
through femur, any level; open, circular (guillotine)' (OMOP 2105211,
standard). Every SNOMED hit for 'guillotine' is unrelated (tonsillectomy,
paper cutter, execution).
This module therefore emits CPT4 for the two guillotine states. BUT the
existing pad_amp_dispo module only ever emits SNOMED-CT / RxNorm / LOINC,
so CPT4 is UNPROVEN through this ETL. Before trusting the guillotine arm:
Rscript workflow/05_etl_csv_to_omop.R  ... then confirm procedure_occurrence
contains OMOP 2105448 / 2105211 for the guillotine patients.
IF THE ETL DROPS CPT4, the guillotine branch cannot be generated faithfully
and acceptance criterion 2 in synthetic_data/registry.yaml (pad_amp v2)
cannot be met without extending the ETL. Do not quietly substitute a
definitive code — that would make the 22-365 day window untestable while
still producing a passing pre-flight.
2. TODO [COMPOSE] This module assumes a BASE module owns the index event and
sets the attributes listed below. Module composition is NOT yet wired:
Step 3 hard-fails on any extra workspace-authored module and Step 4 runs
Synthea with no -m filter, so a per-dataset module manifest is needed first
(see synthetic_data/registry.yaml, pad_amp). Until then, merge these states
into pad_amp_dispo.json as a sub-graph rather than shipping two files.
EXACTLY ONE module may own the index procedure — two modules both emitting
it is what inflated the v1 cohort ~2x (the 379 -> 196 correction).
REQUIRED INPUT ATTRIBUTES (set by the base/index module)
amp_index_level      'TM' | 'TT' | 'TF'   incident level, per the mix above
amp_index_definitive true | false          false = guillotine/disarticulation
index, which selects the 22-365
day window instead of 1-365
OUTPUT ATTRIBUTES set here, for the QC queries:
amp_reamp_occurred, amp_reamp_subtype, amp_reamp_level, amp_death_1y
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: every distribution below is tunable. The four-category
split and the level mix are PUBLISHED and should not be changed without a
reason; the sub-type and timing splits are plausible defaults, not published.
Only patients with an incident amputation enter. Fails closed: if the base
module did not set amp_index_level, nothing here fires and no spurious
progression is emitted.
MoRe's PUBLISHED four-category joint distribution, development sample
n = 7 376. Driving off the JOINT distribution rather than two independent
marginals is deliberate — it makes the death and re-amputation marginals
(19.4% / 28.0%) exact by construction and reproduces the D/R cell, which
an independence assumption would badly under-fill (0.194 x 0.280 = 5.4%
is close here by coincidence, but the strata are not independent in
general and the model's whole point is their joint structure).
DO NOT tune these four without a reason — they are published values.
ND/NR 57.7% — survives 1 year, no re-amputation. The healthiest stratum, and the one 5.2.4's prevalence benchmarks are drawn from.
D/R 5.1% — BOTH outcomes. MoRe: 'it is understood that re-amputation and
death could only be counted if the re-amputation preceded death.' So this
arm must emit the re-amputation FIRST and the death after it. Enforced by
routing through the re-amputation states and only then to Death_After_Reamp.
THE TWO-WINDOW RULE. MoRe uses 1-365 days after a DEFINITIVE index but
22-365 days after a GUILLOTINE or DISARTICULATION index, 'to allow for
revisions within three weeks'.
A cohort SQL that applies one window to both will be wrong in a direction
that depends on which window it picked, and this router is what makes that
detectable.
Definitive index: the qualifying window is 1-365 days. Lower bound 1 day,
not 0 — a same-day second code is part of the index operation, not a
re-amputation.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: the distribution WITHIN the window is not published.
This spans it broadly so a SQL error at either edge is detectable; a
clinically realistic version would be right-skewed toward ~30-90 days.
Guillotine/disarticulation index: window starts at day 22, because days
1-21 are the expected closure of the index operation and are NOT
re-amputations. Day 22 exactly is the boundary case worth having in the
data — an implementation using > 21 and one using >= 22 agree here, but
one using > 22 does not.
Sub-type availability depends on the INCIDENT level, which is the crux of
MoRe's algorithm:
TT / TF  -> all three sub-types (soft tissue revision, same level, higher)
TM       -> NO soft-tissue-revision or same-level codes exist, so any
subsequent TM code IS the same-level re-amputation, and
progression to TT/TF is the higher-level route.
A single sub-type router for all levels would emit TT-only codes for TM
patients and silently make the TM stratum unvalidatable.
TM index. Two routes only.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: 55/45 same-level vs progression is a plausible default,
not published. What matters for validation is that BOTH are non-trivial —
if same-level TM re-amputations are absent, the 'all TM codes count' rule
is never exercised.
TT index — all three sub-types available. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS.
TF index. No higher LE level exists above transfemoral in MoRe's scheme
(hip disarticulation is outside its levels), so only revision and
same-level apply. This asymmetry is real and a uniform sub-type
distribution across levels would be wrong.
Sub-type (a). SNOMED-CT 180048002 'Revision coverage of amputation stump'
-> OMOP 4078404 [vocab query 2026-08-06, standard, Procedure domain].
This is also the 'Maps to' target of ICD-9 84.3, the revision code MoRe's
ref 11 used. TT/TF only — TM has no such code, which is exactly why the
TM branch above bypasses this state.

remarks: Sub-type (c) from TT — the canonical progression MoRe cites (TT -> TF).
QC handle: lets the pre-flight compare emitted re-amputations against what the cohort SQL detects, per-subtype.
MoRe counts a re-amputation that is IPSILATERAL, of UNKNOWN laterality, OR
BILATERAL. Only a confirmed contralateral event is excluded. An
implementation that requires laterality = ipsilateral will UNDER-count, so
the unknown and bilateral arms have to exist in the data to catch that.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS. MoRe: 'Laterality was considered unknown only if none
of the recorded procedures on the same day had laterality.'
TODO [ETL] Synthea has no native procedure-laterality field. Until the ETL
populates procedure_occurrence.modifier_source_value or an ICD-10-PCS
body-part character, these three arms are indistinguishable downstream and
this state is documentation of intent rather than emitted signal.
Enforces MoRe's ordering constraint: in the D/R stratum the re-amputation
must PRECEDE death. Because this router sits AFTER the re-amputation
procedure states, the ordering is structural rather than probabilistic —
it cannot be violated by a distribution change.
D/R: death after the re-amputation but still inside the 365 day outcome
window. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS — the interval is not published.
⚠ Synthea cannot guarantee this stays inside 365 days of the INDEX when the
re-amputation itself landed late in the window, so the QC query must check
death_date <= index + 365 and report the leakage rate rather than assume it
is zero.
D/NR: death within 365 days, no re-amputation. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS — a
realistic curve is front-loaded (peri-operative and early).
Sets death_date, which the ETL writes to the OMOP death table.
v1 had 1 year mortality of 4.0% (8/198); MoRe's is 19.4%. This state plus
the joint distribution is what closes that gap.
NEGATIVE CONTROLS for patients who DID have a qualifying re-amputation.
Adding a non-qualifying event on top tests that the SQL counts the patient
once, not twice.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: 25% get an extra decoy.
ND/NR patients — no qualifying re-amputation. A share of them get an event
that a WRONG implementation would count. These are the patients that make
a false positive visible: if the cohort SQL reports more re-amputations
than amp_reamp_occurred = true, it is counting decoys.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS.
DECOY 1 — inside the guillotine exclusion window. Days 1-21 after a
guillotine/disarticulation index are the expected closure and must NOT
count. A SQL that applies the 1-365 definitive window to guillotine cases
will wrongly count these.
Day 21 is included as the boundary: it must NOT count, while day 22 must.
Same code as a real revision — only the TIMING makes it non-qualifying. That is the point.

remarks: DECOY 2 — CONTRALATERAL amputation inside the 1-365 day window. Correct
timing, correct level, wrong limb: MoRe excludes only confirmed
contralateral events, so this must NOT count.
⚠ Depends on the same laterality gap as Reamp_Laterality_Mix — until the
ETL preserves laterality, this decoy is indistinguishable from a real
ipsilateral re-amputation and will produce a FALSE POSITIVE that looks like
a SQL bug. Resolve TODO [ETL] before scoring this control.

codes.display: Amputation of leg through tibia and fibula [vocab query — OMOP 4338257]

remarks: DECOY 3 — a TOE or RAY amputation in the window. Neither is an incident
level for MoRe (levels are TM/TT/TF only) and neither is 'same or higher
level' than any of them, so neither can be a re-amputation.
This control exists because the workspace's [[minor_amputation]] set
CONTAINS toe and ray, so any SQL built from that broad set rather than from
[[forefoot_midfoot_amputation]] will wrongly count these patients.
See phenotype_library/catalog.yaml — toe_amputation (DVI 1891164) vs
forefoot_midfoot_amputation (DVI 1891165).
SNOMED-CT 371186005 'Amputation of toe' -> OMOP 4159766 [vocab query 2026-08-06]. In toe_amputation, NOT in forefoot_midfoot_amputation.
SNOMED-CT 405443002 'Ray amputation of foot' -> OMOP 4226945 [vocab query
2026-08-06]. A ray removes ONE metatarsal with its toe, so it is NOT a
transmetatarsal amputation (which requires removal of ALL toes) — verified
2026-08-06 that 4226945 is a SIBLING of both the toe and TMA anchors, not a
descendant of either.
